Ratios use nets in contracts, exactly as the CFTC reports them, so a ratio of 1 means equal contract counts, not equal money (a 6E contract is €125,000, a 6J contract ¥12.5m, DX $1,000 × index). A ratio is positive when both legs sit on the same side and negative when they are on opposite sides; it spikes when the quote currency's net is close to zero. Clipped scales the axis to the middle 90% of the visible weeks and marks the weeks beyond it at the edge; Symlog keeps every week in view. COT positions are as of Tuesday; each sits on the price bar of its week (Mon–Fri).
